'''Zhong Lin Wang''' ({{lang-zh|c=王中林|p=Wáng Zhōnglín}}; born November 1961<ref name=cas1>{{Cite web |url=http://casad.cas.cn/sourcedb_ad_cas/zw2/ysxx/wjysmd/200912/t20091203_2681425.html |title=王中林(Zhong Lin Wang) |access-date=2019-06-15 |archive-date=2019-06-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190605032107/http://casad.cas.cn/sourcedb_ad_cas/zw2/ysxx/wjysmd/200912/t20091203_2681425.html}}</ref>) is a Chinese-American physicist, materials scientist and engineer specialized in [[nanotechnology]], energy science and [[electronics]]. He was awarded the [[Albert Einstein World Award of Science]] in 2019, and has been called the 'father of nanogenerators'.

He received his [[PhD]] from [[Arizona State University]] in 1987. He was the Hightower Chair in Materials Science and Engineering and Regents' Professor Chair Emeritus at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]], US.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Zhong Lin Wang {{!}} School of Materials Science and Engineering|url=http://www.mse.gatech.edu/people/zhong-lin-wang/|website=www.mse.gatech.edu/people/zhong-lin-wang}}</ref> In 2024, it was reported that Wang had moved to work in China full-time at the Beijing Institute of Nanoenergy and Nanosystems. It was speculated that this was due to US government persecution of Chinese-American scientists through the [[China Initiative]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-24 |title=Top US scientist and nanotech 'world leader' resigns to work in China |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/china/science/article/3279730/nanotechnology-pioneer-wang-zhonglin-leaves-us-work-china-full-time |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=South China Morning Post |language=en}}</ref>

== Education ==
* Ph.D. in physics, [[Arizona State University]], 1987
* B.S. in Applied Physics, [[Xidian University]], [[Xi'an]], [[China]], 1982

He came to the US for graduate school through [[CUSPEA]] program organized by [[Tsung-Dao Lee]].

== Career ==
Wang was a visiting Lecturer at [[Stony Brook University]] from 1987 to 1988. After working as a research fellow in the following year at [[Cavendish Laboratory]] in the University of Cambridge, Wang joined [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]] and the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]] as a research scientist from 1990 to 1994. He was hired by [[Georgia Institute of Technology]] as an associate professor in 1995; he was promoted to full Professor in 1999, Regents' professor in 2004, and the Hightower Chair in Materials Science and Engineering in 2010. Wang was the Director of the Georgia Tech's Center for Nanostructure Characterization from 2000 to 2015. He is the Founding Director, Director, and Chief Scientist at Beijing Institute of Nanoenergy and Nanosystems, Chinese Academy of Sciences since 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|title=中国科学院北京纳米能源与系统研究所|url=http://www.binn.cas.cn/|website=www.binn.cas.cn}}</ref>

=== Science and technology of nanogenerators ===

Wang worked on piezoelectric nanogenerators in 2006,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wang|first1=Zhong Lin|last2=Song|first2=Jinhui|date=2006-04-14|title=Piezoelectric Nanogenerators Based on Zinc Oxide Nanowire Arrays|journal=Science|volume=312|issue=5771|pages=242–246|doi=10.1126/science.1124005|pmid=16614215 |bibcode=2006Sci...312..242W |s2cid=4810693 |issn=0036-8075}}</ref> for generating electricity from mechanical energy using ZnO nanowire arrays.

Before the invention of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) by Wang in 2011,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fan|first1=Feng-Ru|last2=Tian|first2=Zhong-Qun|last3=Lin Wang|first3=Zhong|date=March 2012|title=Flexible triboelectric generator|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S2211285512000481|journal=Nano Energy|language=en|volume=1|issue=2|pages=328–334|doi=10.1016/j.nanoen.2012.01.004|bibcode=2012NEne....1..328F |s2cid=59434593 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> mechanical energy harvesting mainly relied on the electromagnetic generator (EMG) invented by Faraday in 1831. The EMG is most efficient for high-frequency mechanical motions, such as more than 10–60&nbsp;Hz. The TENGs have advantages over EMG in harvesting low-frequency mechanical energy from the environment. The energy conversion efficiency based on TENG can reach 50-85%.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Xie|first1=Yannan|last2=Wang|first2=Sihong|last3=Niu|first3=Simiao|last4=Lin|first4=Long|last5=Jing|first5=Qingshen|last6=Yang|first6=Jin|last7=Wu|first7=Zhengyun|last8=Wang|first8=Zhong Lin|date=2014-08-25|title=Grating-Structured Freestanding Triboelectric-Layer Nanogenerator for Harvesting Mechanical Energy at 85% Total Conversion Efficiency|journal=Advanced Materials|volume=26|issue=38|pages=6599–6607|doi=10.1002/adma.201402428|pmid=25156128 |bibcode=2014AdM....26.6599X |s2cid=30685667 |issn=0935-9648}}</ref><ref name=":16">{{Cite journal|last1=Zhu|first1=Guang|last2=Zhou|first2=Yu Sheng|last3=Bai|first3=Peng|last4=Meng|first4=Xian Song|last5=Jing|first5=Qingshen|last6=Chen|first6=Jun|last7=Wang|first7=Zhong Lin|date=2014-04-01|title=A Shape-Adaptive Thin-Film-Based Approach for 50% High-Efficiency Energy Generation Through Micro-Grating Sliding Electrification|journal=Advanced Materials|volume=26|issue=23|pages=3788–3796|doi=10.1002/adma.201400021|pmid=24692147 |bibcode=2014AdM....26.3788Z |s2cid=22199444 |issn=0935-9648}}</ref> The maximum output power density obtained so far is up to 500 W/m<sup>2</sup>.<ref name=":16" />

'''Hybrid cell.''' Wang introduced the hybrid cell in 2009 for simultaneously harvesting two or more different types of energy, such as solar and mechanical energy.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Xu|first1=Chen|last2=Wang|first2=Xudong|last3=Wang|first3=Zhong Lin|date=2009-04-01|title=Nanowire Structured Hybrid Cell for Concurrently Scavenging Solar and Mechanical Energies|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=131|issue=16|pages=5866–5872|doi=10.1021/ja810158x|pmid=19338339 |bibcode=2009JAChS.131.5866X |s2cid=40091940 |issn=0002-7863}}</ref>

'''Pyroelectric nanogenerator.''' In 2012, based on the pyroelectric effect, Wang invented the pyroelectric nanogenerator.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yang|first1=Ya|last2=Guo|first2=Wenxi|last3=Pradel|first3=Ken C.|last4=Zhu|first4=Guang|last5=Zhou|first5=Yusheng|last6=Zhang|first6=Yan|last7=Hu|first7=Youfan|last8=Lin|first8=Long|last9=Wang|first9=Zhong Lin|date=2012-06-13|title=Pyroelectric Nanogenerators for Harvesting Thermoelectric Energy|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/nl3003039|journal=Nano Letters|language=en|volume=12|issue=6|pages=2833–2838|doi=10.1021/nl3003039|pmid=22545631 |bibcode=2012NanoL..12.2833Y |issn=1530-6984|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

'''Blue energy.''' In 2014, Wang proposed the idea of blue energy, in which using millions of TENG units to form a TENG network floating on water surface for large-scale wave energy harvesting.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Wang|first=Zhong Lin|date=2014|title=Triboelectric nanogenerators as new energy technology and self-powered sensors – Principles, problems and perspectives|journal=Faraday Discuss.|volume=176|pages=447–458|doi=10.1039/c4fd00159a|pmid=25406406 |bibcode=2014FaDi..176..447W |s2cid=22048783 |issn=1359-6640}}</ref> If one TENG unit can generate a power of 10&nbsp;mW, the total power for the area equal to the size of Georgia state and 10 m depth of water is theoretically predicted to be 16 TW, which can meet the energy needs of the world.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last=Wang|first=Zhong Lin|date=2017-02-09|title=Catch wave power in floating nets|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=542|issue=7640|pages=159–160|doi=10.1038/542159a|pmid=28179678 |bibcode=2017Natur.542..159W |s2cid=4461713 |issn=0028-0836|doi-access=free}}</ref>

'''Theory of nanogenerators from the Maxwell's displacement current'''. In 1861, Maxwell proposed the term ''ε''𝜕𝑬/𝜕𝑡 as the Maxwell's displacement current. Wang suggested adding an additional term 𝜕'''𝑃'''𝑠/𝜕𝑡 into the Maxwell's displacement current for the cases when the surface polarization is present.<ref name=":8">{{Cite journal|last=Wang|first=Zhong Lin|date=February 2020|title=On the first principle theory of nanogenerators from Maxwell's equations|journal=Nano Energy|volume=68|article-number=104272|doi=10.1016/j.nanoen.2019.104272|bibcode=2020NEne...6804272W |s2cid=210249178 |issn=2211-2855}}</ref><ref name=":17"/> Recently, Wang has proposed expanding Maxwell's equations for moving charged media.<ref name=":9">{{Cite journal|last=Wang|first=Zhong Lin|date=December 2021|title=On the expanded Maxwell's equations for moving charged media system – General theory, mathematical solutions and applications in TENG|journal=Materials Today|volume=52 |pages=348–363 |doi=10.1016/j.mattod.2021.10.027|s2cid=245105522 |issn=1369-7021}}</ref>

'''Origins of [[Triboelectric effect|contact electrification]].''' Wang has argued<ref name=":10">{{Cite journal|last1=Xu|first1=Cheng|last2=Zi|first2=Yunlong|last3=Wang|first3=Aurelia Chi|last4=Zou|first4=Haiyang|last5=Dai|first5=Yejing|last6=He|first6=Xu|last7=Wang|first7=Peihong|last8=Wang|first8=Yi-Cheng|last9=Feng|first9=Peizhong|last10=Li|first10=Dawei|last11=Wang|first11=Zhong Lin|date=April 2018|title=On the Electron-Transfer Mechanism in the Contact-Electrification Effect|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/adma.201706790|journal=Advanced Materials|language=en|volume=30|issue=15|article-number=1706790|doi=10.1002/adma.201706790|pmid=29508454 |bibcode=2018AdM....3006790X |s2cid=3757981 |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Xu|first1=Cheng|last2=Wang|first2=Aurelia Chi|last3=Zou|first3=Haiyang|last4=Zhang|first4=Binbin|last5=Zhang|first5=Chunli|last6=Zi|first6=Yunlong|last7=Pan|first7=Lun|last8=Wang|first8=Peihong|last9=Feng|first9=Peizhong|last10=Lin|first10=Zhiqun|last11=Wang|first11=Zhong Lin|date=2018-08-09|title=Raising the Working Temperature of a Triboelectric Nanogenerator by Quenching Down Electron Thermionic Emission in Contact-Electrification|journal=Advanced Materials|volume=30|issue=38|article-number=1803968|doi=10.1002/adma.201803968|pmid=30091484 |bibcode=2018AdM....3003968X |s2cid=51940860 |issn=0935-9648|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Wang|first1=Zhong Lin|last2=Wang|first2=Aurelia Chi|date=November 2019|title=On the origin of contact-electrification|journal=Materials Today|volume=30|pages=34–51|doi=10.1016/j.mattod.2019.05.016|s2cid=189987682 |issn=1369-7021}}</ref> that electron transfer between atoms/molecules in contact electrification is due to electron cloud overlap (or wave function overlap) between the repulsive region, because interatomic potial barrier can be reduced.  Then, a hybrid layer model has been proposed to reveal the formation process of electric double layer between liquid and solid.<ref name=":11">{{Cite journal|last1=Lin|first1=Shiquan|last2=Chen|first2=Xiangyu|last3=Wang|first3=Zhong Lin|date=2021-06-23|title=Contact Electrification at the Liquid–Solid Interface|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.chemrev.1c00176|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=122 |issue=5 |language=en|pages=5209–5232|doi=10.1021/acs.chemrev.1c00176|pmid=34160191 |s2cid=235609525 |issn=0009-2665|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The photon emission due to interface electron transfer and transition has been observed, resulting in the birth of the contact-electrification induced emission spectroscopy (CEIIS).<ref name=":12">{{Cite journal|last1=Li|first1=Ding|last2=Xu|first2=Cheng|last3=Liao|first3=Yanjun|last4=Cai|first4=Wenzhe|last5=Zhu|first5=Yongqiao|last6=Wang|first6=Zhong Lin|date=2021-09-24|title=Interface inter-atomic electron-transition induced photon emission in contact-electrification|journal=Science Advances|volume=7|issue=39|article-number=eabj0349 |doi=10.1126/sciadv.abj0349|pmid=34559569 |pmc=8462885 |bibcode=2021SciA....7..349L |s2cid=237628400 |issn=2375-2548}}</ref> Furthermore, the electron transfer between liquid and solid surfaces can be used for contact-electro catalysis (CEC).<ref name=":13">{{Cite journal|title=Contact-electro-catalysis for the Degradation of Organic Pollutants Using Pristine Dielectric Powder|journal=Nature Communications|bibcode=2022NatCo..13..130W |last1=Wang |first1=Ziming |last2=Berbille |first2=Andy |last3=Feng |first3=Yawei |last4=Li |first4=Site |last5=Zhu |first5=Laipan |last6=Tang |first6=Wei |last7=Wang |first7=Zhong Lin |year=2022 |volume=13 |issue=1 |page=130 |doi=10.1038/s41467-021-27789-1  |doi-access=free|pmid=35013271 |pmc=8748705 |s2cid=245839613 }}</ref>

'''Energy for the new era and high entropy energy.''' Wang proposed the idea of "energy for the new era" in 2017 to distinguish the distributed energy sources from the well-known new energy.<ref name=":17">{{Cite journal |last1=Wang |first1=Zhong Lin |last2=Jiang |first2=Tao |last3=Xu |first3=Liang |date=September 2017 |title=Toward the blue energy dream by triboelectric nanogenerator networks |journal=Nano Energy |volume=39 |pages=9–23 |doi=10.1016/j.nanoen.2017.06.035 |bibcode=2017NEne...39....9W |issn=2211-2855}}</ref> Recently, Wang studied the entropy theory of energy distribution and utilization for the era of internet of things.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Wang|first=Zhong Lin|date=April 2019|title=Entropy theory of distributed energy for internet of things|journal=Nano Energy|volume=58|pages=669–672|doi=10.1016/j.nanoen.2019.02.012|bibcode=2019NEne...58..669W |s2cid=139527230 |issn=2211-2855}}</ref> The "ordered" energy transmitted from power plants is used to solve the "ordered" applications for fixed sites and part of "disordered" distributed power applications, while the "disordered" energy harvested from the environment is mainly to solve distributed applications.

=== Piezotronics and piezo-phototronics of the third generation semiconductors ===

'''Piezotronic effect and piezotronics'''''.'' When applying a stress on a material with a non-centrosymmetric crystal structure, a piezoelectric potential ''(piezopotential)'' can be produced. For a ZnO nanowire, the Schottky barrier height between the nanowire and its metal contact can be effectively tuned by the created internal field. Such phenomenon is called as the ''piezotronic effect'', which was discovered by Wang in 2007.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last=Wang|first=Z. L.|date=2007-03-19|title=Nanopiezotronics|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/adma.200602918|journal=Advanced Materials|language=en|volume=19|issue=6|pages=889–892|doi=10.1002/adma.200602918|bibcode=2007AdM....19..889W |url-access=subscription}}</ref> The field of ''piezotronics'' represents the electronics in which the piezopotential acts as a gate voltage.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wu|first1=Wenzhuo|last2=Wen|first2=Xiaonan|last3=Wang|first3=Zhong Lin|date=2013-05-24|title=Taxel-Addressable Matrix of Vertical-Nanowire Piezotronic Transistors for Active and Adaptive Tactile Imaging|journal=Science|volume=340|issue=6135|pages=952–957|doi=10.1126/science.1234855|pmid=23618761 |bibcode=2013Sci...340..952W |s2cid=206547682 |issn=0036-8075|doi-access=free}}</ref> Recently, the piezotronic effect in 2D materials was also demonstrated.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wu|first1=Wenzhuo|last2=Wang|first2=Lei|last3=Li|first3=Yilei|last4=Zhang|first4=Fan|last5=Lin|first5=Long|last6=Niu|first6=Simiao|last7=Chenet|first7=Daniel|last8=Zhang|first8=Xian|last9=Hao|first9=Yufeng|last10=Heinz|first10=Tony F.|last11=Hone|first11=James|date=October 2014|title=Piezoelectricity of single-atomic-layer MoS2 for energy conversion and piezotronics|journal=Nature|volume=514|issue=7523|pages=470–474|doi=10.1038/nature13792|pmid=25317560 |bibcode=2014Natur.514..470W |s2cid=4448528 |issn=0028-0836}}</ref>

'''Piezo-phototronic effect and piezo-phototronics.''' When applying a strain, the piezopotential created by interface polarization charges can greatly tune the local band structure and shift the charge depletion zone at a pn junction. The separation or recombination of charge carriers at the junction can be enhanced as excited by photon. Such phenomenon is called as the ''piezo-phototronic effect'', discovered by Wang in 2009,<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last1=Hu|first1=Youfan|last2=Chang|first2=Yanling|last3=Fei|first3=Peng|last4=Snyder|first4=Robert L.|last5=Wang|first5=Zhong Lin|date=2010-01-15|title=Designing the Electric Transport Characteristics of ZnO Micro/Nanowire Devices by Coupling Piezoelectric and Photoexcitation Effects|journal=ACS Nano|volume=4|issue=2|pages=1234–1240|doi=10.1021/nn901805g|pmid=20078071 |issn=1936-0851}}</ref> in which the optoelectronic processes are tuned and controlled by the created piezopotential. By using this effect, the pressure/force [[sensor array]]s based on individual-nanowire LED have been fabricated, which can map strain at a high resolution and density<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pan|first1=Caofeng|last2=Dong|first2=Lin|last3=Zhu|first3=Guang|last4=Niu|first4=Simiao|last5=Yu|first5=Ruomeng|last6=Yang|first6=Qing|last7=Liu|first7=Ying|last8=Wang|first8=Zhong Lin|date=2013-08-11|title=High-resolution electroluminescent imaging of pressure distribution using a piezoelectric nanowire LED array|journal=Nature Photonics|volume=7|issue=9|pages=752–758|doi=10.1038/nphoton.2013.191|bibcode=2013NaPho...7..752P |s2cid=4128581 |issn=1749-4885}}</ref> and enhance the efficiency of LED.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yang|first1=Qing|last2=Liu|first2=Ying|last3=Pan|first3=Caofeng|last4=Chen|first4=Jun|last5=Wen|first5=Xiaonan|last6=Wang|first6=Zhong Lin|date=2013-01-24|title=Largely Enhanced Efficiency in ZnO Nanowire/p-Polymer Hybridized Inorganic/Organic Ultraviolet Light-Emitting Diode by Piezo-Phototronic Effect|journal=Nano Letters|volume=13|issue=2|pages=607–613|doi=10.1021/nl304163n|pmid=23339573 |bibcode=2013NanoL..13..607Y |issn=1530-6984}}</ref>

'''Piezophotonic effect.''' Wang theoretically predicted the piezoelectric-induced photon-emission effect (piezophotonic effect) in 2008.<ref name=":6">{{Cite journal|last=Wang|first=Zhong Lin|date=2008-11-24|title=Towards Self-Powered Nanosystems: From Nanogenerators to Nanopiezotronics|journal=Advanced Functional Materials|volume=18|issue=22|pages=3553–3567|doi=10.1002/adfm.200800541|s2cid=43937604 |issn=1616-301X}}</ref> The photo emission can occur, resulting from the drop of trapped charges from the vacancy/surface states back to the valence band, under the existence of the piezoelectric potential'''.''' Such effect has been experimentally observed and verified in his later work.<ref name=":7">{{Cite journal|last1=Wang|first1=Xiandi|last2=Zhang|first2=Hanlu|last3=Yu|first3=Ruomeng|last4=Dong|first4=Lin|last5=Peng|first5=Dengfeng|last6=Zhang|first6=Aihua|last7=Zhang|first7=Yan|last8=Liu|first8=Hong|last9=Pan|first9=Caofeng|last10=Wang|first10=Zhong Lin|date=2015-02-25|title=Dynamic Pressure Mapping of Personalized Handwriting by a Flexible Sensor Matrix Based on the Mechanoluminescence Process|journal=Advanced Materials|volume=27|issue=14|pages=2324–2331|doi=10.1002/adma.201405826|pmid=25711141 |bibcode=2015AdM....27.2324W |s2cid=205259440 |issn=0935-9648}}</ref>

'''Tribotronics.''' The field of ''tribotronics'' represents the electronics in which the triboelectric acts as a gate voltage.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Zhang|first1=Chi|last2=Tang|first2=Wei|last3=Zhang|first3=Limin|last4=Han|first4=Changbao|last5=Wang|first5=Zhong Lin|date=2014-08-26|title=Contact Electrification Field-Effect Transistor|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/nn5039806|journal=ACS Nano|language=en|volume=8|issue=8|pages=8702–8709|doi=10.1021/nn5039806|pmid=25119657 |issn=1936-0851|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

=== Growth and understanding ZnO nanostructures ===

Wang discovered oxide nanobelts in 2001.<ref name=":15">{{Cite journal|last1=Pan|first1=Z. W.|last2=Dai|first2=Z. R.|last3=Wang|first3=Z. L.|date=2001-03-09|title=Nanobelts of semiconducting oxides|journal=Science|volume=291|issue=5510|pages=1947–1949|doi=10.1126/science.1058120|issn=0036-8075|pmid=11239151|bibcode=2001Sci...291.1947P |s2cid=16880233 }}</ref>

=== In-situ nanomeasurements in TEM ===

In 1999 Wang and co-workers used transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to measure the properties of individual carbon nanotubes, including the mechanical, electrical and field emission ones.<ref name=":14">{{Cite journal|last1=Poncharal|first1=Philippe|last2=Wang|first2=Z. L.|last3=Ugarte|first3=Daniel|last4=de Heer|first4=Walt A.|date=1999-03-05|title=Electrostatic Deflections and Electromechanical Resonances of Carbon Nanotubes|journal=Science|volume=283|issue=5407|pages=1513–1516|doi=10.1126/science.283.5407.1513|pmid=10066169 |bibcode=1999Sci...283.1513P |issn=0036-8075}}</ref> Wang demonstrated a nanobalance technique and an approach toward nanomechanics.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gao|first1=Ruiping|last2=Wang|first2=Zhong L.|last3=Bai|first3=Zhigang|last4=de Heer|first4=Walter A.|last5=Dai|first5=Liming|last6=Gao|first6=Mei|date=2000-07-17|title=Nanomechanics of Individual Carbon Nanotubes from Pyrolytically Grown Arrays|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=85|issue=3|pages=622–625|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.85.622|pmid=10991355 |bibcode=2000PhRvL..85..622G |hdl=1853/9276 |issn=0031-9007|hdl-access=free}}</ref>

=== Theory of inelastic scattering in electron diffraction and imaging ===

Wang did some research to understand inelastic scattering in electron diffraction and imaging. He published a textbook on ''Elastic and Inelastic Scattering in Electron Diffraction and Imaging'' (Plenum Press, 1995)<sup>[27]</sup>. In scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), the high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) (referred as Z-contrast) is dominated by the thermal diffuse scattering (TDS) and a dynamic theory for including TDS in image simulation of HAADF was proposed.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wang|first1=Z.L.|last2=Cowley|first2=J.M.|date=December 1989|title=Simulating high-angle annular dark-field stem images including inelastic thermal diffuse scattering|journal=Ultramicroscopy|volume=31|issue=4|pages=437–453|doi=10.1016/0304-3991(89)90340-9|issn=0304-3991}}</ref>
